title: Introduce secure toolchain connector harness quickstart
author: Samir Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a new quickstart demonstrating a secure connector pattern for agent tool-calling: ephemeral credential exchange, policy-enforced tool bindings, and local replay proxy for dev/testing.
body:
Motivation: Customers building agents with tool-calling asked for a small, security-first quickstart that demonstrates how to wire a connector (external API or internal microservice) into a RAG/agent workflow while preserving least-privilege access, auditability, and deterministic local testing. This PR adds a compact 'Secure Toolchain Connector Harness' quickstart that stitches together: ephemeral credential issuance, policy-based tool bindings, a local replay proxy for deterministic dev/eval, and examples for telemetry hooks and structured output checks.

What this includes (single continuous description): The quickstart contains a step-by-step README, a minimal connector adapter (TypeScript), a local proxy that records and replays connector invocations, example policy JSON schema and policy-enforcer middleware, CI smoke tests, and a short notebook demonstrating an agent flow that calls the connector for factual data augmentation. The narrative focuses on security trade-offs: short-lived tokens, scope-limited connector roles, and how to combine Redwood's function/tool-calling API with gateway-level RBAC.

Checklist: - [x] Add quickstart scaffold and README with architecture diagram and security guidance - [x] Implement connector adapter (ts) + auth shim - [x] Add local replay proxy and recorded fixtures for deterministic runs - [x] Instrument telemetry probes for connector latency and per-call cost - [x] Add end-to-end smoke tests to CI and a GitHub Actions job to validate replay fixtures - [x] Update docs index (quickstarts list) and link to the new page - [x] Add Linear references and basic release notes

Commits (high-level): ["init: add secure connector quickstart scaffold", "feat(connector): implement auth shim + ephemeral token flow", "test: add replay proxy and fixtures", "docs: quickstart README and security guidance", "ci: add smoke test job and matrix", "fix: tighten policy-enforcer error handling", "chore: small test flake fixes and formatting"]

Changed areas (high level): ["redwood-quickstarts/secure-connector-harness/README.md","redwood-quickstarts/secure-connector-harness/connector-adapter/src/index.ts","redwood-quickstarts/secure-connector-harness/replay-proxy/index.ts","redwood-quickstarts/secure-connector-harness/policies/example-policy.json","redwood-quickstarts/secure-connector-harness/tests/e2e/smoke.test.ts","redwood-quickstarts/secure-connector-harness/fixtures/recorded-calls.json","docs/quickstarts/index.yml",".github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml"]

Small snippets included in the PR: The adapter exports a single callConnector function that accepts an ephemeral token and an input payload; the policy-enforcer rejects requests with mismatched scopes. The replay proxy stores requests and responses in fixtures/ and exposes a --record flag for fresh captures.

Review conversation (summary): Marina Chen: "High level LGTM — the pattern here is useful. A couple of comments: (1) make the default token TTL shorter in the examples, (2) add a note in README about production KMS/HSM integration for signing ephemeral tokens, and (3) can we fail fast in the policy-enforcer when scopes are absent?" Samir (author): "Thanks Marina — reduced default TTL to 60s in the example, added KMS note, and updated enforcer to fail fast with an explicit 401 and audit log entry." Omar Delgado: "Two suggestions: include a sample of how to run the replay proxy with insecure-mode for local-only debugging, and add a check in CI that the recorded fixtures haven't drifted unexpectedly." Samir: "Added --insecure-dev flag and a CI job that runs the smoke test against recorded fixtures and fails on mismatch hashes." Lena Voss: "Please add one short paragraph to the README about how to adapt the connector to on-prem services that require mutual TLS." Samir: "Added mTLS guidance and an example curl command in the README."

CI summary and timeline: First run (Actions job quickstart-smoke) failed due to a flaky test around timing in the replay proxy. I pushed a small timing-lock fix and re-ran CI. Second run passed all jobs (unit, lint, smoke matrix) — logs are linked in the PR checks. A lightweight security review verified that no long-lived demo credentials are checked in.

Usage and testing notes for reviewers: - Quickstart can be launched with `yarn && yarn dev` inside the quickstart directory; the README has a three-step flow (issue ephemeral token -> run agent example -> inspect telemetry). - The replay proxy supports `--record` and `--replay` modes; the smoke CI runs in replay mode to ensure hermetic tests. - The connector adapter is intentionally minimal: production integrations should swap the in-memory token signer for a KMS-backed signer and replace demo policies with org-specific RBAC rules.

Why this is different from other quickstarts: Existing examples illustrate agent orchestration and tool-calling, but many assume connectors are trusted long-term or don't demonstrate secure credential exchange and dev-time replay. This quickstart fills that gap by showing end-to-end flows (dev -> CI -> prod) and surface-level telemetry to validate connector economics.

Follow-ups planned (linked ENG tickets): - ENG-8220: Add a Go adapter variant and a Python example for platform SDK parity - ENG-8221: Extend the policy-enforcer to support attribute-based access controls (ABAC) - PM-403: Collate quickstarts into an 'operational patterns' doc and add a short workshop

Merge: Squash and merge with a concise commit message "quickstarts: secure toolchain connector harness (ephemeral auth + replay)". The PR was merged after approvals from Marina and Omar and CI green.

notes_for_maintainers: This quickstart intentionally keeps secrets out of source. Example token signer is in-memory and clearly marked; do not use in production. If backporting docs, update the quickstarts index to point to the v2 examples page.
how_to_verify_locally: cd redwood-quickstarts/secure-connector-harness && yarn && yarn dev; open http://localhost:3000 and follow README steps to issue a short-lived token, run agent example, then run replay-proxy with --replay to assert recorded fixtures.
